papers.title: Accelerated Diffusion Models via Speculative Sampling
papers.authors: Valentin De Bortoli*, Alexandre Galashov*, Arthur Gretton, Arnaud Doucet (* equal contribution; all Google DeepMind)
papers.venue: ICML 2025, PMLR 267:12590-12631 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/de-bortoli25a.html); arXiv v1 9 Jan 2025, v2 6 Jul 2025 (HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05370v2); OpenReview https://openreview.net/forum?id=BTJSkPpH1t
papers.key_algorithm: TARGET = the K-step Euler-Maruyama chain of the reverse SDE with churn eps>0: q(y_k|y_{k-1}) = N(y_k; m^q_{k-1}(y_{k-1}), sigma_{k-1}^2 I), m^q_k(y) = y + gamma*b^q_{t_k}(y), sigma_k = sqrt(gamma)*eps*g_{1-t_k}, gamma = 1/K, b_t(x) = -f_{1-t}x + (1+eps^2)/2 * g_{1-t}^2 * s_{1-t}(x). DRAFT = any Gaussian kernel with the SAME sigma_k: p(y_k|y_{n:k-1}) = N(m^p_{k-1}(y_{n:k-1}), sigma_{k-1}^2 I). Draft options: (i) INDEPENDENT cheaper DDM b^p; (ii) FROZEN TARGET draft: m^p_k = y_k + gamma*b^q_{t_n}(y_n), i.e. the target drift is computed once at the window start and reused for all L steps (one target call per window, no training, draft steps can be sampled in parallel); (iii) App. B: an 'efficient frozen' variant that reuses b^q_{t_n}(y~_n), which was already computed during the previous verification, so drafting costs no target call after the first (later named the 'Free Drafter'); a Medusa-like learned correction c_theta(x_s,x_t); convex mixtures of drafts; ParaDiGMS Picard output used as the draft. Algorithm 3/6: Y_0 ~ N(0,I), n = 0; loop: n_L = min(n+L, K); (Seq.) draw Y~_{n+1:n_L} from the draft; (Par.) compute the target means m^q_{k-1}(Y~_{k-1}) for every k in the window in ONE batched call; for k = n+1..n_L run REJECTION(p_k, q_k, Y~_k) (also vectorised); stop at the first rejection (keep its corrected state and discard the rest of the draft); n <- k.
papers.acceptance_rule: Algorithm 4, reflection maximal coupling (Bou-Rabee et al. 2020). Delta = (m^p - m^q)/sigma, e = Delta/||Delta||, Z = (Y~ - m^p)/sigma, U ~ Unif[0,1]. Accept if U <= min(1, N(Z+Delta;0,I)/N(Z;0,I)), which equals q(Y~)/p(Y~); otherwise set Y = m^q + sigma*(I - 2ee^T)Z. That reflection is deterministic and needs no extra target call. Prop 3.1: Y ~ q exactly, and P(Y != Y~) = ||p-q||_TV = 2*Phi(||m^p-m^q||/(2 sigma)) - 1, which is maximal. There is one U per step for the WHOLE d-dimensional state. Temperature variant (Alg. 7): the ratio is taken under N(.;0,tau I). tau > 1 raises acceptance but is NOT exact: Prop F.1 shows it acts as guidance toward the draft; tau < 1 pushes toward the target. Sec 3.2: sampling the classical residual max(0, q-p) by rejection costs on average at least one target sample, and its variance blows up as p -> q (the stated reason for using reflection). App. E: with different covariances, acceptance goes to about 0 in high dimension.
papers.speedup_mechanism: One batched target call verifies up to L drafted transitions. NFE is defined as a call to the target with a batch, whatever the batch size. Prop 4.1 (independent draft): E[C_orig/C_spec] = E[L^]/(1 + L*C_p/C_q). This helps iff E[L^]/L >= C_p/C_q + 1/L, and with per-step acceptance >= alpha, E[L^] >= 1 - alpha^L + L*alpha^(L+1). Lemma 4.2: E[a_n] >= exp(-E||Delta_n||^2/2), where ||Delta_n||^2 = gamma/4 * (eps + 1/eps)^2 * g^2 * ||s^p - s^q||^2. So acceptance rises with a small step (large K), the bound is best at eps about 1, and acceptance is high at early noisy steps. The paper reports only NFE, no wall-clock. Its limitations section notes that deterministic samplers are not covered, that parallel calls add memory overhead, and that diffusion models are not memory-bound, so parallel verification is not free.
papers.reported_results: CIFAR-10 pixel U-Net, 100-step target, FROZEN draft (Table 1). Exact (tau=1), eps=0.25: FID 2.35 / IS 10.25 at 39.31 target NFE, vs FID 2.45 for the 100-step target and 7.68 for a 30-step target. The headline 'FID 2.34 with 35 calls (-65%)' uses tau=2.0 (35.40 NFE), which is NOT exact. Other exact settings: eps=0.01 -> 61.64 NFE; eps=0.5 -> 40.37; eps=1.0 -> 44.81. LSUN 64x64: 'around halving the NFE' (App. J, window 50, 100/200/500-step targets). Latent CIFAR-10 (4x4x32): about 3x fewer NFE (window 15). PushT diffusion policy (tau=1, frozen): L=20, K=100 gives reward 0.898+-0.008 at 27.2 NFE vs 0.889 at 100; L=10, K=10 gives 0.903 at 5.05 NFE. Combined with ParaDiGMS (CIFAR-10, 30 steps): FID 2.23 at 15.69 NFE -> 2.07 at 15.42. The window L used for Table 1 is not stated in the main text (UNVERIFIED).
papers.code_url: No official code: the arXiv v2 HTML and the PMLR PDF contain no code or GitHub statement (both checked). A third-party implementation of the same chain verifier (reflection maximal coupling, K=1) is at https://github.com/marcellobullo/tree-specdiff
papers.contact_emails: vdebortoli@google.com. The paper prints 'Correspondence to: Valentin De Bortoli <vdebortoli@google.com>' (ICML PDF, arXiv v1 and v2). No other author email is printed.
papers.relevance: Baseline for action item 2. spec_v0 --specstep already uses Algorithm 4, but per latent position (16-dim) rather than on the whole state. Kernels factorise over positions, so this is exact for a single transition, but it gives no lookahead: the speed-up needs the whole state to be accepted for several consecutive steps. The target must be a stochastic K-step chain (eps>0) with the same sigma_k as the draft, and exactness holds only with respect to that discretised chain.

papers.title: Accelerating Speculative Diffusions via Block Verification
papers.authors: Alexander Soen (work done at Google), Hisham Husain, Valentin De Bortoli, Arnaud Doucet. Listed affiliations are KTH, Google Research and Google DeepMind; the per-author mapping is UNVERIFIED.
papers.key_algorithm: (1) 'Decomposition' residual: an exact one-shot sampler for r(y) proportional to max{0, alpha*q(y) - p(y)} with equal-covariance Gaussians (Prop 3.1). Draw U ~ psi_alpha, a 1-D law with closed-form CDF Psi_alpha(u) = [alpha*Phi(u) - Phi(u - ||Delta||)] / [alpha*Phi(log(alpha)/||Delta|| + ||Delta||/2) - Phi(log(alpha)/||Delta|| - ||Delta||/2)] for u below log(alpha)/||Delta|| + ||Delta||/2 (inverted by bisection). Draw Z_perp ~ N(0, I - ee^T). Set Y = m^q + sigma*(U*e + Z_perp). This implements the original (Gamma-maximal) speculative residual with a single target evaluation. (2) Block verification (Sun et al. 2025) carried over to diffusion, with the generalised residual r_BLOCK proportional to max{0, alpha_{tau-1} q(y|y^_{k+tau-1}) - p(y|y^_{k:k+tau-1})}. Prop 3.2: no deterministic, reflection-style residual can be valid under block verification when the draft length is 2 or more. (3) Free Drafter: a frozen drafter that reuses the target drift computed in the previous verification.
papers.acceptance_rule: Block verification maximises the joint acceptance of the whole draft block. The output is exactly the target DDPM chain (the theorem of Sun et al. 2025 is recovered).
papers.speedup_mechanism: The gamma+1 draft states are verified in parallel. Under ideal conditions the Frozen Drafter speed-up is about be/(2+eps) (be = block efficiency), because the drafter itself costs one target call. The Free Drafter reaches about be/(1+eps+eps'). Acceptance falls as sigma_k -> 0 (late steps), and the speed-up grows with the number of steps K.
papers.reported_results: K=250, gamma=7 (CelebA, CIFAR10, LSUN, ImageNet pixel and latent; Cloud TPU v3): 1.9-3.6x wall-clock over DDPM, with block verification adding 1.5-6.3% over reflection. ImageNet LDM, eps=0.5, gamma=7: 1.22x (K=50), 1.55x (100), 2.20x (250), 2.90x (500), about 3.8x (1000); FID matches DDPM. The Frozen Drafter has higher block efficiency but 7-24% lower wall-clock speed-up than the Free Drafter.
papers.contact_emails: None found in the arXiv HTML (UNVERIFIED)
papers.relevance: Offers an exact residual sampler if block verification is wanted. The quantitative lesson is that exact speculative diffusion pays off only with many stochastic steps and a nearly free drafter. At K of about 50-70 (Base's reference uses 70 steps), expect about 1.2-1.5x wall-clock even with ideal parallel verification.

papers.title: Diffusion Models are Secretly Exchangeable: Parallelizing DDPMs via Autospeculation
papers.authors: Hengyuan Hu, Aniket Das, Dorsa Sadigh, Nima Anari
papers.key_algorithm: Autospeculative Decoding (ASD). Via stochastic localization, DDPM increments are exchangeable after reparametrisation. One model call at step a is used to propose the means of all future steps; the paper states this corresponds to De Bortoli's frozen target draft. Verification uses a Gaussian rejection sampler with reflection coupling, in O(1).
papers.acceptance_rule: min(1, q/p) on Gaussian transitions, with the reflection on rejection. The paper states that the output is 'identically distributed as sequential samples from the DDPM' (error-free).
papers.speedup_mechanism: Theory: O~(K^{2/3}) parallel calls, i.e. an O~(K^{1/3}) speed-up. In practice each speculative step runs on its own GPU ('speculation length = number of parallel GPUs').
papers.reported_results: 1.8-4x wall-clock overall. Stable Diffusion v2 (1000-step DDPM): 1.51-1.82x wall-clock (1.51-1.90x algorithmic) with speculation length 2-8. Pixel LSUN Church 256: up to 3.1x algorithmic, 2.13-2.51x wall-clock. Robomimic: about 4x. CLIP, FID and success rates unchanged.
papers.contact_emails: hengyuan.hhu@gmail.com, aniketd@stanford.edu (printed in the arXiv HTML)
papers.relevance: Independent, concurrent proof that frozen/self drafting is exact. Parallel verification is realised as one GPU per speculative step. With a 14B video DiT and our GPUs 4-7, the speculation length is capped at 4.

papers.title: Accelerating Diffusion Sampling via Speculative Draft Trees
papers.authors: Marcello Bullo, Yanxiao Liu, Öykü Sıla Güner, Arpan Mukherjee, Deniz Gündüz (Imperial College London)
papers.key_algorithm: Links speculative diffusion to relative entropy coding. Uses K-ary draft trees instead of a chain; children are i.i.d. proposals with a 'delayed drift' (the target drift at the root is frozen during drafting). Verification is greedy rejection sampling (D-GRS), with a fall-back to the normalised residual.
papers.acceptance_rule: D-GRS over each node's children, which gives exact target samples. The reflection maximal coupling chain is the special case K=1.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Spends a parallel budget B of target evaluations per round on width rather than depth.
papers.reported_results: Up to 8.3% faster and 14% fewer target NFE than the reflection chain; about 1.18x on FFHQ and SD3 (512x512 latent, d=65,536). The authors state that the draft-target mean discrepancy scales with sqrt(d) and that exact coupling efficiency degrades rapidly with dimension (an open problem).
papers.relevance: Warns about dimension: a LingBot chunk has about 295k latent dimensions (16x3x58x106), so accepting the whole state is hopeless unless the drafter is almost identical to the target. The repo is the only public code for the De Bortoli chain verifier.

papers.title: Parallel Sampling via Autospeculation
papers.authors: Nima Anari, Carlo Baronio, CJ Chen, Alireza Haqi, Frederic Koehler, Anqi Li, Thuy-Duong Vuong
papers.key_algorithm: Speculative rejection sampling with an 'autospeculative' proposal built from the same oracle, covering any-order AR models and diffusion (conditional-mean oracle).
papers.acceptance_rule: Rejection sampling with the target as the exact output law (high-accuracy regime; assumes bounded support).
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel oracle calls: expected time O~(n^{1/2}) instead of O~(n).
papers.reported_results: Theory only.
papers.relevance: Theoretical backing that exact parallel or speculative diffusion sampling is possible. Not directly practical for us.

papers.title: Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models (ParaDiGMS)
papers.authors: Andy Shih, Suneel Belkhale, Stefano Ermon, Dorsa Sadigh, Nima Anari
papers.key_algorithm: Picard (fixed-point) iterations over a sliding window of denoising steps. Future states are guessed and every step in the window is refined in parallel until the error drops below a tolerance. Works with DDIM, DPM-Solver and DDPM (with the noise fixed in advance).
papers.acceptance_rule: Convergence tolerance, not accept/reject. Converges to the sequential trajectory for the same noise; the output is equal to the sequential sample only up to the tolerance.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Trades parallel compute (a batch of steps per iteration) for fewer sequential rounds.
papers.reported_results: 2-4x; 0.2 s for 100-step DiffusionPolicy and 14.6 s for 1000-step StableDiffusion-v2, with no measurable drop in reward, FID or CLIP.
papers.relevance: The main parallel (non-speculative) baseline. It needs many cheap steps; for a 14B video DiT each Picard sweep is a batch of 14B forwards (compute-bound).

papers.title: Accelerating Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models (ParaTAA)
papers.authors: Zhiwei Tang, Jiasheng Tang, Hao Luo, Fan Wang, Tsung-Hui Chang
papers.key_algorithm: Casts sampling as a triangular nonlinear system solved by fixed-point iteration, sped up with Anderson-type acceleration.
papers.acceptance_rule: Fixed-point convergence; produces 'the same images as the sequential sampling'.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel steps per iteration; 4-14x fewer sequential steps.
papers.reported_results: SD with 100-step DDIM: the same image in 7 parallel inference steps.
papers.relevance: A Picard-family baseline; exact only in the limit (the deterministic fixed point).

papers.title: Accelerating Diffusion Models with Parallel Sampling: Inference at Sub-Linear Time Complexity
papers.authors: Haoxuan Chen, Yinuo Ren, Lexing Ying, Grant M. Rotskoff
papers.key_algorithm: O(1) blocks with parallel Picard iterations inside each block, for both SDE and probability-flow ODE.
papers.acceptance_rule: None; the analysis bounds the error with respect to the continuous process (generalised Girsanov).
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel Picard iterations.
papers.reported_results: Theory: O~(poly log d) time complexity.
papers.relevance: Theory for the Picard family; the result is approximate (bounded error), not exact.

papers.title: Self-Refining Diffusion Samplers: Enabling Parallelization via Parareal Iterations (SRDS)
papers.authors: Nikil Roashan Selvam, Amil Merchant, Stefano Ermon
papers.key_algorithm: Parareal: a coarse, cheap solve produces a rough sample, which is then refined in parallel across the trajectory by fine solves.
papers.acceptance_rule: None; guaranteed to converge to the serial ODE solution.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel-in-time refinement.
papers.reported_results: Up to 1.7x on 25-step SD-v2 and up to 4.3x on longer trajectories.
papers.relevance: A conceptual cousin of plan->render (coarse plan, then refine). It is exact only at convergence and for an ODE.

papers.title: Continuous Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Image Generation (CSpD)
papers.authors: Zili Wang, Robert Zhang, Kun Ding, Qi Yang, Fei Li, Shiming Xiang
papers.venue: The arXiv comment says ECCV 2026, while Soen et al. cite it as NeurIPS 2024 (venue UNVERIFIED)
papers.key_algorithm: Speculative decoding for continuous-token AR models with diffusion heads (MAR, xAR, Harmon). The density ratio of a continuous token is approximated by 'denoising trajectory alignment': draft and target head trajectories share the reparametrisation noise, and the ratio reduces to the last-step Gaussians times a product of variance ratios. Adds 'token pre-filling' (about 5% of tokens from the target) and samples the residual max(0, p-q) by acceptance-rejection with an upper bound.
papers.acceptance_rule: min(1, target/draft) on an approximate last-step likelihood ratio. The residual step is exact, but the ratio is a proxy, so the method is not exactly target-distributed (UNVERIFIED wording).
papers.speedup_mechanism: The target verifies a draft of 32 continuous tokens in parallel.
papers.reported_results: MAR-H 2.33x, xAR-H 2.72x, Harmon-1.5B 2.54x; FID essentially unchanged (MAR-H 2.35 -> 2.36).
papers.contact_emails: smxiang@nlpr.ia.ac.cn (corresponding author, per the arXiv HTML)
papers.relevance: The closest published idea to token- or frame-level speculative acceptance with a diffusion-generated continuous unit. Its trick (shared noise plus a last-step Gaussian ratio) is a template for a chunk-level test, but it is approximate.

papers.title: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Video Generation (SDVG)
papers.authors: Yuezhou Hu*, Jintao Zhang* (UC Berkeley)
papers.key_algorithm: Block-level draft-verify for block-causal video diffusion. Drafter: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B Self-Forcing. Target: Krea Realtime Video 14B (Self-Forcing distilled from Wan2.1-14B). Both run 4 denoising steps per block with t = [1000, 937, 833, 625, 0] (the same grid as LingBot Fast), 9 blocks x 3 latent frames at 832x480. Each draft block is VAE-decoded and scored with ImageReward using the MIN over frames. Block 0 is always regenerated by the target. The drafter's KV cache is updated unconditionally; an accepted draft is committed to the target's KV cache; the VAE decode cache is cloned before scoring and restored on rejection.
papers.acceptance_rule: Deterministic threshold: accept if min_i ImageReward(frame_i) >= tau (tau = -0.7 by default). On rejection the target regenerates the block from the same initial noise. The authors state explicitly that this is NOT exact: 'SDVG accepts a distributional shift toward the drafter'.
papers.speedup_mechanism: The draft is 3.77x faster; accepted blocks skip the target entirely.
papers.reported_results: 1003 MovieGenVideoBench prompts, 2x RTX A6000. Target-only: VisionReward 0.0788, 97.0 s. SDVG tau=-0.7: 0.0773 (98.1%), 60.9 s, 1.59x, 73.1% accepted. tau=-2.5: 0.0754, 2.09x, 88.9% accepted. Draft-only: 0.0644, 3.77x. Random routing at a matched rate gives 0.0706.
papers.code_url: No SDVG repo found; the paper cites https://github.com/krea-ai/realtime-video for the target model
papers.relevance: The only published draft-verify method for AR video diffusion. Setup is very close to ours (4-node grid, chunk KV commit). It is biased and uses a reward proxy, so it is the natural 'learned/proxy verifier' baseline for action item 5, not an unbiased method.

papers.title: Speculative Coupled Decoding for Training-Free Lossless Acceleration of Autoregressive Visual Generation (earlier title: MC-SJD, Maximal Coupling Speculative Jacobi Decoding)
papers.authors: Junhyuk So, Hyunho Kook, Chaeyeon Jang, Eunhyeok Park
papers.key_algorithm: Speculative Jacobi decoding in which the draft tokens of consecutive Jacobi iterations are sampled with a maximal (or Gumbel) coupling, maximising the chance that the same token is re-drawn, which stabilises the draft context and raises acceptance.
papers.acceptance_rule: Standard speculative acceptance; the paper claims the final output distribution matches the target model ('lossless').
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel Jacobi drafts verified by the same model.
papers.reported_results: Up to 4.2x on images and up to 13.6x on video (Cosmos-1-AR-4B, discrete tokens, RealEstate10k, windows 16-128) with no FVD degradation.
papers.relevance: Lossless speculative decoding for AR VIDEO, but with discrete tokens. The idea to transfer is coupling (common random numbers) across draft and verify, which reflection coupling already does in the continuous case.

papers.title: Accelerating Auto-regressive Text-to-Image Generation with Training-free Speculative Jacobi Decoding (SJD)
papers.authors: Yao Teng, Han Shi, Xian Liu, Xuefei Ning, Guohao Dai, Yu Wang, Zhenguo Li, Xihui Liu
papers.key_algorithm: Jacobi parallel decoding of token windows with a probabilistic convergence criterion; the previous Jacobi iterate serves as the draft distribution.
papers.acceptance_rule: A speculative-sampling-style probabilistic criterion. Whether SJD itself claims exact losslessness is UNVERIFIED; SCD, which builds on it, claims lossless.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Several tokens are accepted per forward pass.
papers.reported_results: About 2x fewer steps on AR T2I models (exact numbers not checked).
papers.relevance: Self-speculative (no draft model) parallel decoding for visual AR. Follow-up SJD2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08994) adds noise-initialised tokens refined by Jacobi denoising; per our check it makes no exactness claim.

papers.title: LANTERN: Accelerating Visual Autoregressive Models with Relaxed Speculative Decoding
papers.authors: Doohyuk Jang, Sihwan Park, June Yong Yang, Yeonsung Jung, Jihun Yun, Souvik Kundu, Sung-Yub Kim, Eunho Yang
papers.key_algorithm: Relaxed speculative acceptance for visual AR, which accepts draft tokens that are close in latent space to likely target tokens.
papers.acceptance_rule: Relaxed and NOT exact (a controlled distribution shift).
papers.speedup_mechanism: Higher acceptance through relaxation.
papers.reported_results: Not checked (UNVERIFIED).
papers.relevance: Example of a deliberately biased 'relaxed' acceptance, analogous to De Bortoli's tau>1.

papers.title: Playing with Transformer at 30+ FPS via Next-Frame Diffusion
papers.authors: Xinle Cheng, Tianyu He, Jiayi Xu, Junliang Guo, Di He, Jiang Bian
papers.key_algorithm: Action-conditioned next-frame diffusion world model with 'speculative sampling': the next few frames are generated assuming the current action persists, and are discarded if the incoming action differs.
papers.acceptance_rule: Accept the pre-generated frames iff the actual action equals the assumed action. Lossless in the trivial sense of prefetching (the same computation as sequential); UNVERIFIED beyond the abstract.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Hides latency by prefetching.
papers.reported_results: More than 30 FPS on an A100 (with other optimisations).
papers.relevance: The only 'speculative' mechanism found in a video world model; it is exact but not a draft/target model pair.

papers.title: Fast Autoregressive Video Generation with Diagonal Decoding (DiagD)
papers.authors: Yang Ye, Junliang Guo, Haoyu Wu, Tianyu He, Tim Pearce, Tabish Rashid, Katja Hofmann, Jiang Bian
papers.key_algorithm: Training-free decoding of token-based AR video models along spatio-temporal diagonals, parallel within a frame and partially overlapping consecutive frames.
papers.acceptance_rule: None; approximate, with a speed-quality trade-off.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel token decoding.
papers.reported_results: Up to 10x with comparable fidelity.
papers.relevance: Frame-overlap parallelism for AR video; not exact.

papers.title: SRDiffusion: Accelerate Video Diffusion Inference via Sketching-Rendering Cooperation
papers.authors: Shenggan Cheng, Yuanxin Wei, Lansong Diao, Yong Liu, Bujiao Chen, Lianghua Huang, Yu Liu, Wenyuan Yu, Jiangsu Du, Wei Lin, Yang You
papers.key_algorithm: The large model runs the high-noise steps (sketch: semantics and motion); the small model runs the low-noise steps (render). A metric decides when to switch.
papers.acceptance_rule: None; approximate.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Replaces the large model with the small one on the low-noise steps.
papers.reported_results: Over 3x for Wan with nearly no VBench loss, 2x for CogVideoX, 6.22x combined with TeaCache and SageAttention.
papers.relevance: Closest published analogue of our plan->render (Base plans, Fast renders); should be cited in related work. Not unbiased.

papers.title: T-Stitch: Accelerating Sampling in Pre-Trained Diffusion Models with Trajectory Stitching
papers.authors: Zizheng Pan, Bohan Zhuang, De-An Huang, Weili Nie, Zhiding Yu, Chaowei Xiao, Jianfei Cai, Anima Anandkumar
papers.key_algorithm: The small model runs the early steps and the large model the later steps.
papers.acceptance_rule: None; approximate.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Model switching along the trajectory.
papers.reported_results: DiT-XL: 40% of early steps replaced by a 10x faster DiT-S without an FID drop.
papers.relevance: The opposite ordering to SRDiffusion and our plan->render. Useful for related work.

papers.title: FREE: Uncertainty-Aware Autoregression for Parallel Diffusion Transformers
papers.authors: Xinwan Wen, Bowen Li, Jiajun Luo, Ye Li, Zhi Wang
papers.key_algorithm: A lightweight drafter autoregresses DiT features across denoising steps, with parallel verification by the DiT.
papers.acceptance_rule: Claims 'lossless acceleration' (the exact rule is UNVERIFIED); a 'relax' variant uses uncertainty to relax acceptance.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Feature-level drafting, verified in parallel.
papers.reported_results: ImageNet-512: 1.86x lossless, 2.25x relaxed.
papers.relevance: A learned lightweight drafter for a DiT's own denoising chain; a candidate drafter if Base's own chain were run speculatively.

papers.title: Judge Decoding: Faster Speculative Sampling Requires Going Beyond Model Alignment
papers.authors: Gregor Bachmann, Sotiris Anagnostidis, Albert Pumarola, Markos Georgopoulos, Artsiom Sanakoyeu, Yuming Du, Edgar Schönfeld, Ali Thabet, Jonas Kohler
papers.venue: ICLR 2025 (as cited by Soen et al.)
papers.key_algorithm: Trains a small 'judge' head on target embeddings to accept correct but low-likelihood draft tokens.
papers.acceptance_rule: A learned verifier; deliberately NOT exact.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Higher acceptance.
papers.reported_results: Not checked (UNVERIFIED).
papers.relevance: Precedent for the 'learned lightweight verifier' in action item 5.

papers.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding / Accelerating LLM Decoding with Speculative Sampling
papers.authors: Leviathan, Kalman, Matias (ICML 2023); Chen, Borgeaud, Irving, Lespiau, Sifre, Jumper (arXiv 2302.01318, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01318)
papers.key_algorithm: The draft proposes L tokens; the target scores them in one parallel pass; tokens are accepted sequentially; the first rejection is resampled from max(0, q-p).
papers.acceptance_rule: min(1, q/p), with residual max(0, q-p), which gives exact target samples.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Memory-bound LLM decoding makes the L-token verify pass about as cheap as one step.
papers.reported_results: 2-3x for LLMs.
papers.relevance: Definition of exactness that the diffusion versions inherit. Sun et al. (SpecTr, https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15141) identified it as a maximal coupling; block verification (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444) is its joint-acceptance improvement.

papers.title: Speculative Sampling For Faster Molecular Dynamics (Langevin Speculative Dynamics)
papers.authors: Arthur Kosmala, Stephan Günnemann, Meng Gao, Brandon Wood
papers.key_algorithm: The draft model proposes fast Langevin steps; the slow target verifies them in parallel and applies a transport map from draft to target.
papers.acceptance_rule: Claims theoretically and empirically that sampled trajectories follow the target model (the coupling details are UNVERIFIED).
papers.speedup_mechanism: Parallel verification.
papers.relevance: A trajectory-level (time-series) application of De Bortoli-style exact speculation, structurally closest to frame-by-frame rollouts.

papers.title: TS-DP: Reinforcement Speculative Decoding for Temporal Adaptive Diffusion Policy Acceleration
papers.authors: Ye Li, Jiahe Feng, Yuan Meng, Kangye Ji, Chen Tang, Xinwan Wen, Shutao Xia, Zhi Wang, Wenwu Zhu
papers.key_algorithm: A distilled Transformer drafter for diffusion-policy denoising calls, plus an RL scheduler that adapts the speculative parameters over time.
papers.acceptance_rule: Described as 'lossless' speculative decoding (the exact rule is UNVERIFIED).
papers.speedup_mechanism: The drafter replaces base denoising calls.
papers.reported_results: Up to 4.17x, over 94% of drafts accepted, 25 Hz.
papers.relevance: Adaptive (time-varying) speculation parameters for sequential decision rollouts.

papers.title: Self-Speculative Masked Diffusions
papers.authors: Andrew Campbell, Valentin De Bortoli, Jiaxin Shi, Arnaud Doucet
papers.key_algorithm: Discrete masked diffusion whose final attention layer is made causal, giving non-factorised draft predictions validated in the same forward pass (model-integrated speculative sampling).
papers.acceptance_rule: Speculative acceptance on discrete tokens.
papers.speedup_mechanism: About 2x fewer forward passes.
papers.reported_results: About 2x NFE reduction on GPT2-scale text and protein sequences.
papers.relevance: Same group; the 'self-speculative' idea (the target drafts for itself) for the discrete case.

papers.title: Fast-ARDiff: An Entropy-informed Acceleration Framework for Continuous Space Autoregressive Generation
papers.authors: Zhen Zou, Xiaoxiao Ma, Jie Huang, Zichao Yu, Feng Zhao
papers.key_algorithm: Entropy-informed speculative decoding for AR-diffusion hybrids (continuous tokens), plus a distilled few-step diffusion head.
papers.acceptance_rule: Residual sampling by rejection in continuous space, according to Soen et al.'s characterisation.
papers.speedup_mechanism: Draft and target AR, with a few-step head.
papers.reported_results: TransDiff 4.3x 'lossless'; NextStep-1 3x.
papers.relevance: Another continuous AR speculative method; its losslessness claim is not independently verified.

notes:
WHAT 'EXACT / UNBIASED' MEANS IN EACH FAMILY (item 4)
- LLM speculative decoding (Leviathan; Chen): output tokens have exactly the target's autoregressive distribution at the given temperature.
- De Bortoli 2025, ASD (Hu 2025), block verification (Soen 2026), draft trees (Bullo 2026): exact with respect to the target's DISCRETISED STOCHASTIC chain. That chain is K Euler-Maruyama or DDPM steps with churn eps>0, on the same time grid and the same per-step noise std sigma_k as the draft. It is not exact with respect to the continuous-time model or to any other sampler (for example a 70-step ODE/UniPC reference).
- Conditions for exactness: tau=1 only (tau>1 is biased toward the draft, Prop F.1); equal covariances (with unequal ones acceptance is about 0 in high dimension, App. E); target means evaluated at the accepted previous state; the rest of the draft discarded after the first rejection. Deterministic samplers are not supported.
- Picard / Parareal family (ParaDiGMS, ParaTAA, Chen 2024, SRDS): converge to the sequential trajectory for fixed noise. They are exact only at convergence or up to a tolerance, or come with error bounds.
- CSpD: exact residual step, but the acceptance ratio is an approximation (aligned trajectories, last-step Gaussian).
- SCD / MC-SJD: lossless on discrete tokens.
- SDVG, LANTERN, Judge decoding, SRDiffusion, T-Stitch, DiagD: explicitly biased.
- NFD 'speculative sampling': trivially lossless action prefetch.

DE BORTOLI DETAILS ASKED FOR (item 2)
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05370, ICML 2025, PMLR 267:12590-12631.
- Draft: any Gaussian kernel with the same sigma_k. The recommended one is the FROZEN target drift b^q_{t_n}(y_n), reused for L steps. Its 'efficient' form reuses the drift from the previous verification (Soen et al. call it the Free Drafter and show it is 7-24% faster in wall-clock than frozen).
- Target kernel: N(y + gamma*b^q_t(y), gamma*eps^2*g^2 I).
- Acceptance: U <= min(1, N(Z+Delta)/N(Z)), for the whole state.
- Rejection: Y = m^q + sigma(I - 2ee^T)Z, deterministic, needs no extra call.
- Speed-up: one batched target call verifies up to L steps, measured in NFE only. Exact result: CIFAR-10 FID 2.35 at 39.3 NFE vs 2.45 at 100. The 2.34 at 35 headline uses tau=2 and is not exact.
- Code: none released. Third-party chain implementation: https://github.com/marcellobullo/tree-specdiff (rmc, K=1).
- Email as printed: vdebortoli@google.com ('Correspondence to: Valentin De Bortoli'). This is the only address on the paper.
- Follow-up by the same group: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13426 (exact Gamma-residual, block verification, Free Drafter; ImageNet LDM wall-clock 1.22x at K=50 and 1.55x at K=100).

IMPLICATIONS FOR spi0 (my analysis, not from a paper; check before relying on it)
1) The current --specstep (spec_v0.py L473-492) matches Algorithm 4, but per 16-dim latent position. That is exact for each verified transition, because both kernels factorise over positions. What it certifies is a surrogate target chain:
   - 4-node x0-renoise at Fast's sigmas;
   - Base x0 with the RePaint-renoised prefix and one CFG forward;
   - the final node-3 x0 (the committed output) is Fast's own and unverified, since the last step is deterministic and cannot be coupled.
   So the output is not a sample of Base's 70-step distribution, and not of a block-causal Base either.
2) There is no speed-up path at the current granularity. Lookahead needs the WHOLE chunk state to be accepted, with probability 2*Phi(-||Delta||/2), where ||Delta|| sums over about 18.4k positions x 16 channels. A per-position |d| of 0.34 (the CPU-check value) gives ||Delta|| of about 46, so acceptance is about 0. Bullo et al. report the same sqrt(d) degradation.
3) In x0-renoise kernels the per-position Delta equals (1-s)/s * |x0_D - x0_T|. The factor is 0.064, 0.205 and 0.587 for transitions into nodes 1, 2 and 3. Early transitions are accepted almost regardless of disagreement. This is the churn/eps trade-off of Lemma 4.2 and Thm 4.3.
4) Base's 70-step chain run speculatively. Fast is a poor drafter for it: different grid, 4 nodes, block-causal. The literature's best drafter is the target itself (frozen or free drafter). The sampler must become an SDE (eps>0).
   - Parallel verification of gamma+1 states is not free on a compute-bound 14B DiT (18-32k tokens), so it means one GPU per speculative step, as in ASD. That is at most 4 with GPUs 4-7.
   - Expected wall-clock at K=70 is about 1.2-1.5x (from Soen Table 3 and ASD Fig. 2). Speculative sampling cannot close the 600 s -> ~100 s gap by itself.
5) Frame- or chunk-level exact AR acceptance: I found NO published exact method for continuous AR video chunks. Exact chunk acceptance needs p_T(chunk|prefix):
   - Base is bidirectional, so this conditional is undefined without marginalising future frames. The exact target must be a block-causal Base (specwm/base_cache.py) or the whole-clip Base chain.
   - Path-space ratios over shared-noise trajectories are computable. But the path residual can only be sampled by per-step coupling (which reduces to De Bortoli) or by rejection, which costs at least a sequential target run (De Bortoli Sec 3.2).
   - Closest published approximations: CSpD (last-step likelihood ratio) and SDVG (reward router, biased).
6) Related work to cite for plan->render: SRDiffusion (large sketch, small render; https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19151), SRDS (coarse then parallel refine), T-Stitch. Pipelined or diagonal frame denoising (not speculative) is relevant to item 6: FIFO-Diffusion https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11473 and Diffusion Forcing https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01392. Also not speculative for video: SpeCa, speculative feature caching (https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11628, details UNVERIFIED), and SCOPE, AR-video frame caching and extrapolation (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02979, approximate). Christopher et al., Speculative Diffusion Decoding (https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05636), uses discrete diffusion as an LLM drafter and has low relevance.
